facts.raw_span: progressive unilateral skin hardening on his right thigh and buttock for 7 years
motion of his right limb joint was slightly limited
ill-defined, stony-hard plaque involving his right thigh above the patella extending to his right buttocks with loss of skin elasticity
mild hypertrichosis and hyperpigmentation
Normal results for routine blood tests
Normal results for autoantibodies, immunoglobulins, C-reactive protein, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
slight thickening of subcutaneous tissue and T2 signal abnormality on MRI of right thigh
Normal epidermis and mild pigmentation along the basal layer with subtle increase in density of fibroblasts extending to the subcutis and forming adipocyte entrapment but no evidence of inflammation
Increased expression of CD34 in the reticular dermis
Negative Alcian blue staining
Dense reticular dermis extended below well-preserved appendages
no evidence of inflammation

concepts.why: The patient's progressive unilateral skin hardening, ill-defined plaque, and loss of skin elasticity, along with the histopathological findings of increased density of fibroblasts and dense reticular dermis, are consistent with scleroderma.
The patient's unilateral skin hardening, ill-defined plaque, and hypertrichosis are consistent with morphea, a form of localized scleroderma.

rationales.F01: Unilateral skin hardening is more typical of Morphea than Scleroderma.
rationales.F02: Limited joint motion is not specific to either condition.
rationales.F03: The ill-defined, stony-hard plaque is more characteristic of Morphea.
rationales.F04: Mild hypertrichosis and hyperpigmentation are not specific to either condition.
rationales.F05: Normal blood tests do not differentiate between the conditions.
rationales.F06: Normal autoantibody results are less typical of Scleroderma.
rationales.F07: Slight thickening of subcutaneous tissue and T2 signal abnormality on MRI could be seen in Morphea.
rationales.F08: The histopathological findings are more consistent with Morphea.
rationales.F09: Increased expression of CD34 in the reticular dermis could be seen in Morphea.
rationales.F10: Negative Alcian blue staining does not differentiate between the conditions.
rationales.F11: Dense reticular dermis extended below well-preserved appendages is more characteristic of Morphea.
rationales.F12: No evidence of inflammation is more typical of Morphea.
